info.title: Adding request ID tracking to FastAPI

messages.text:
In the FastAPI source directory (fastapi/), add a built-in mechanism for automatic request ID tracking.

1. Open fastapi/applications.py and inspect the FastAPI class constructor and the `build_middleware_stack` flow.
2. Add a new optional parameter `add_request_id_header: bool = False` to the `FastAPI.__init__()` signature.
3. When `add_request_id_header=True`, inject a middleware that:
   - Generates a UUID4 for each incoming request.
   - Attaches it as `X-Request-ID` to the response headers.
   - Makes it accessible as `request.state.request_id`.
4. Write a test in tests/test_request_id_middleware.py that:
   - Creates `FastAPI(add_request_id_header=True)`.
   - Verifies `X-Request-ID` is present in response headers.
   - Verifies it is a valid UUID4 string.
5. Run `pytest -W ignore tests/test_request_id_middleware.py` and ensure all tests pass.

## graphify

This project has a knowledge graph at graphify-out/ with god nodes, community structure, and cross-file relationships.

Rules:
- For codebase questions, first run `graphify query "<question>"` when graphify-out/graph.json exists. Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts. These return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.
- If graphify-out/wiki/index.md exists, use it for broad navigation instead of raw source browsing.
- Read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context.
- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).

161: This step has two parts: **structural extraction** (deterministic, free) and **semantic extraction** (LLM, costs tokens).

163: > **graphify needs no API key. Never ask the user for one, and never block on one.** Code is extracted structurally (AST) with no LLM and no key at all — a code-only corpus (the common `/graphify .` on a repo) skips semantic extraction entirely, so it needs nothing here: go straight to Part A and skip Part B. Semantic extraction (only for docs, papers, and images) uses Gemini **only if** `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` is already set; otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM. graphify does **not** read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or any other provider key. If you catch yourself about to prompt for, wait on, or stop because of a missing API key, that is a misread of this skill — proceed without one.

165: **Before semantic extraction:** check whether `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is set. If neither is set, print this one-liner to the user:
166: > Tip: set `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` to use Gemini for semantic extraction (`pip install 'graphifyy[gemini]'`).

If `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` IS set, use `graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel(files, backend="gemini")` for semantic extraction instead of dispatching subagents. The default Gemini model is `gemini-3-flash-preview`; set `GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL` or pass `--model` in headless CLI flows to override it.

170: > **No other API keys are read.** When `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` are unset, semantic extraction falls to the host agent itself — the running session is the LLM. On a host that dispatches subagents (e.g. Claude Code), dispatch them as written in Part B. On a host that runs the CLI directly in a terminal and cannot dispatch subagents, do not stall: a code-only corpus has no semantic work, so write the empty semantic file (Part B "Fast path") and continue to Part C; for a corpus with docs/papers/images, either set a Gemini key or extract those inline yourself, but in no case prompt for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — that prompt is a misread of this skill.

255: **Step B1 - Split into chunks**
256: 
257: Load files from `graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt`. Split into chunks of 20-25 files each. Each image gets its own chunk (vision needs separate context). When splitting, group files from the same directory together so related artifacts land in the same chunk and cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted.

259: **Step B2 - Dispatch ALL subagents in a single message**
260: 
261: Call the Agent tool multiple times IN THE SAME RESPONSE - one call per chunk. This is the only way they run in parallel. If you make one Agent call, wait, then make another, you are doing it sequentially and defeating the purpose.
262: 
263: **IMPORTANT - subagent type:** Always use `subagent_type="general-purpose"`. Do NOT use `Explore` - it is read-only and cannot write chunk files to disk, which silently drops extraction results. General-purpose has Write and Bash access which the subagent needs.
264: 
265: Concrete example for 3 chunks:
266: ```
267: [Agent tool call 1: files 1-15, subagent_type="general-purpose"]
268: [Agent tool call 2: files 16-30, subagent_type="general-purpose"]
269: [Agent tool call 3: files 31-45, subagent_type="general-purpose"]
270: ```
271: All three in one message. Not three separate messages.
272: 
273: Each subagent receives this exact prompt (substitute FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE, and CHUNK_PATH).
274: 
275: CHUNK_PATH must be an **absolute** path — derive it before dispatching:
276: ```bash

278: # Then for chunk N: CHUNK_PATH="${PROJECT_ROOT}/graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_0N.json"
279: ```

281: Subagent prompt template:
282: 
283: See `references/extraction-spec.md` for the exact subagent prompt (JSON schema, node-ID rules, confidence rubric, frontmatter, hyperedge, and vision rules). Load it only here, only when at least one chunk holds a doc, paper, or image; a pure-code corpus has skipped Part B and never reads it. Pass each subagent that prompt verbatim with FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE, and CHUNK_PATH substituted, and have it write the result to CHUNK_PATH.

285: **Step B3 - Collect, cache, and merge**

288: - Check that `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json` exists on disk — this is the success signal
289: - If the file exists and contains valid JSON with `nodes` and `edges`, include it and save to cache
290: - If the file is missing, the subagent was likely dispatched as read-only (Explore type) — print a warning: "chunk N missing from disk — subagent may have been read-only. Re-run with general-purpose agent." Do not silently skip.
291: - If a subagent failed or returned invalid JSON, print a warning and skip that chunk - do not abort

293: If more than half the chunks failed or are missing, stop and tell the user to re-run and ensure `subagent_type="general-purpose"` is used.

import uuid
from typing import Any

from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders
from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send


class RequestIDMiddleware:
    """
    ASGI middleware that automatically generates a unique request ID for each
    incoming HTTP request, attaches it to the response as the ``X-Request-ID``
    header, and makes it accessible as ``request.state.request_id`` from within
    route handlers.

    The request ID is a UUID4 string (e.g. ``"81eba082-1032-4c47-aa93-a41b7324fa98"``).
    This is useful for correlating logs, traces, and error reports across
    services.

    Non-HTTP scopes (such as WebSocket connections and lifespan events) are
    passed through untouched.
    """

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        # Generate a fresh UUID4 for this request. A new ID is generated for
        # every incoming HTTP request so that downstream code can correlate
        # the entire request lifecycle (logs, traces, error reports) under
        # a single identifier.
        request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

        # Make the request ID available as ``request.state.request_id`` from
        # within route handlers. ``Request.state`` is backed by ``scope["state"]``,
        # so storing it here makes it visible to any subsequent ``Request``
        # instance created from the same scope (including the one FastAPI's
        # router constructs for the route handler).
        request = Request(scope, receive=receive)
        request.state.request_id = request_id

        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                headers = MutableHeaders(scope=message)
                headers["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
            await send(message)

        await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)

import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient


@pytest.fixture
def app_with_request_id() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(add_request_id_header=True)

    @app.get("/echo-request-id")
    def echo_request_id(request: Request) -> dict[str, str | None]:
        return {"request_id": getattr(request.state, "request_id", None)}

    @app.post("/echo-body")
    def echo_body(payload: dict) -> dict:
        return payload

    @app.get("/notfound")
    def notfound() -> dict:
        from fastapi.exceptions import HTTPException

        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="nope")

    return app


@pytest.fixture
def app_without_request_id() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI()

    @app.get("/")
    def root() -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"hello": "world"}

    return app


def test_request_id_header_present(app_with_request_id: FastAPI) -> None:
    client = TestClient(app_with_request_id)
    response = client.get("/echo-request-id")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "x-request-id" in response.headers


def test_request_id_header_is_valid_uuid4(app_with_request_id: FastAPI) -> None:
    client = TestClient(app_with_request_id)
    response = client.get("/echo-request-id")
    assert response.status_code == 200

    header_value = response.headers["x-request-id"]
    # uuid.UUID(...) raises ValueError if the string is not a valid UUID.
    parsed = uuid.UUID(header_value)
    # UUID version 4 means random-based; this is the only format we generate.
    assert parsed.version == 4


def test_request_id_header_format(app_with_request_id: FastAPI) -> None:
    """A UUID4 string is 36 characters: 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits with dashes."""
    client = TestClient(app_with_request_id)
    response = client.get("/echo-request-id")
    header_value = response.headers["x-request-id"]
    assert len(header_value) == 36
    # The canonical form is lowercase; verify our generator produces it that way.
    assert header_value == header_value.lower()


def test_request_id_unique_per_request(app_with_request_id: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Each request must get its own fresh UUID4."""
    client = TestClient(app_with_request_id)
    first = client.get("/echo-request-id").headers["x-request-id"]
    second = client.get("/echo-request-id").headers["x-request-id"]
    assert first != second


def test_request_id_exposed_in_request_state(app_with_request_id: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Route handlers should see the same ID via request.state.request_id."""
    client = TestClient(app_with_request_id)
    response = client.get("/echo-request-id")
    body = response.json()
    header_value = response.headers["x-request-id"]
    assert body["request_id"] == header_value


def test_request_id_on_post_request(app_with_request_id: FastAPI) -> None:
    client = TestClient(app_with_request_id)
    response = client.post("/echo-body", json={"hello": "world"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "x-request-id" in response.headers
    assert uuid.UUID(response.headers["x-request-id"]).version == 4


def test_request_id_header_absent_by_default(
    app_without_request_id: FastAPI,
) -> None:
    """Without the flag, no X-Request-ID header is added."""
    client = TestClient(app_without_request_id)
    response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "x-request-id" not in response.headers
